questiontext.text:
Goal

An inn records a guest's name and stay length when it accepts a booking. The Lighthouse Inn assigns the room only when the guest arrives. Record a booking before it has a room number.

Read
  • Struct types. Read the first paragraph. What does a struct contain? Skip the grammar box and inspect the Go example. How does it declare one field?
  • Composite literals. Read the first paragraph and find Struct literals. What does a key identify inside a struct literal?
  • Composite literals, the same heading. Find the rule for an element list with keys. What value does an omitted field receive?
Coming from Java

A Java record's canonical constructor requires every component. An unknown room therefore needs a value such as -1 or null. Go has no null value for an int.

record Booking(String guest, int nights, int room) {}
Booking b = new Booking("Ada", 3, -1);
Stuck? Two nudges inside
  • Read the rule about keyed struct literals before adding any placeholder value.
  • The declarations above the Struct literals examples show how to name a struct type.

Goal

A theatre ticket identifies the performance and seat that a visitor bought. The Playhouse usher compares two tickets at the door and rejects duplicates. The box office also keeps unused blank tickets. Write checks for both cases.

Read
  • Comparison operators. Find the bullet about struct types. Which struct types are comparable? When are two struct values equal? Which fields does Go compare?
  • Composite literals. Read the rules above Struct literals. What value does a literal with no elements produce?
  • Composite literals, the paragraph about a parsing ambiguity. What must you add when a composite literal appears between if and the opening brace?
Coming from Java

A Java developer might use a record's equals and hashCode, or compare two toString results. A Go struct has no equals method to override.

record Ticket(String holder, String seat, boolean paid) {}
boolean same = a.toString().equals(b.toString());
Required: ==
Stuck? Two nudges inside
  • Find corresponding in the struct bullet. How does Go pair the fields of a with those of b?
  • For blank, find the Composite literals rule for a literal without an element list.

expected.text: {Ada Lovelace B4 true} {Ada Lovelace B4 true} false

questiontext.text:
Goal

A shelf tag shows the stored details for one product. Nuts and Bolts Ltd prints one for every product, but names entered by hand often produce incorrect tags. Create one function that prepares every product before printing. It strips the spaces around the name and records an empty unit as each. It also spells out mm, m, kg, and g as millimetre, metre, kilogram, and gram, with a space before the word. On the tag, an each product reads sold singly and aisle 0 reads not yet shelved.

Read
  • strings.NewReplacer. Read the signature and first sentence. What prefix starts the function name? What type does the call return? How do you supply an old string and its replacement?
  • strings.NewReplacer, the same doc comment. If two old strings match at the same position, which one does the Replacer use?
  • strings.TrimSpace. Which characters does it remove? From which ends of the string?
Coming from Java

A Java constructor might assign this.name = name.trim() and store replacements in a Map with no meaningful entry order. Go has no constructors and no this.

public Product(String name, String unit, int aisle) {
    this.name = expand(name.trim());
    this.unit = unit.isEmpty() ? "each" : unit;
}
Stuck? Two nudges inside
  • Find argument order in the NewReplacer documentation. Which of the abbreviations in the Goal start with the same letter?
  • Find where TrimSpace looks for white space. Which space in the finished tag must the Replacer add?
